subject: System Design
title: Crash Failures vs Byzantine Failures
description: A quick win: understand Crash Failures vs Byzantine Failures.

hook.text: A crashed node is predictable: it stops responding. A Byzantine node is unpredictable: it lies.

buildup.text: Crash-stop failures mean a node simply stops. It doesn't send wrong data or corrupt messages.

discovery.text: Byzantine failures include bugs that produce wrong results, hardware that flips bits, or malicious actors.

twist.text: Most internal systems only handle crash failures. Byzantine tolerance is 10x more expensive in complexity.

climax.text: Know your failure model. Over-engineering for Byzantine faults wastes effort in trusted environments.

punchline.text: Crashed is predictable. Byzantine is chaotic. Design accordingly.

quiz.question: What makes Byzantine failures harder to handle?
options: Faulty nodes can send wrong or contradictory information
